description: Equipo mexicano conformado por miembros activos del Centro Universitario de Ciencias Exactas e Ingenierías (CUCEI) de la Universidad de Guadalajara.
summary:
Our project is an educational space exploration game inspired by Snakes and Ladders and Zathura, set on the planet Mars. Players take on the role of a rover exploring the Martian surface and discovering nine objects and technologies related to the exploration of this planet.

We developed the game in two formats: a physical board game and a digital prototype. Both feature a 30-space board divided into three types of spaces: regular spaces, story spaces, and special event spaces. In the physical version, story and special event spaces are represented by two separate decks of cards. Players randomly draw a card from the corresponding deck depending on the space they land on. In the digital version, landing on one of these spaces opens a separate screen that randomly displays the corresponding story or event.

The project aims to make Mars exploration accessible to a wider audience through an interactive experience that combines gameplay, storytelling, and scientific information. We believe it is important to transform data and achievements from space missions into engaging and accessible experiences that spark curiosity about science, technology, and space exploration.
details:
Our project is an educational space exploration game that works similarly to a traditional board game, but it comes in two formats: a physical version and a digital version. Both share the same rules and mechanics, allowing players to move across a 30-space board while discovering information about nine objects and technologies related to the exploration of Mars. During the game, players can land on three types of spaces: regular spaces, story spaces, and special event spaces. In the physical version, special spaces are resolved using two separate decks of cards, while in the digital version, additional screens appear to randomly display a story or an event, depending on the space where the player lands.

The project's main benefits include encouraging collaboration, social interaction, and communication among participants. It is designed as a shared activity that invites people to interact and enjoy an experience together. Our expected impact is to make space exploration accessible to a wider audience through an entertaining and engaging experience. We believe that fun can be a valuable tool for facilitating learning, as people can develop greater curiosity and interest in scientific topics when they are presented in an interactive and recreational way.

To develop the project, we used various tools and resources, including HTML for programming the digital version, Canva for designing and creating visual materials, BeepBox for audio creation, Google Drive for team organization and collaboration, Pinterest for visual references, and artificial intelligence models such as ChatGPT and Claude as support tools throughout the creative and development process. We also used information and resources provided by NASA as the scientific foundation for the game's content.

The project's creativity lies in combining two complementary formats, physical and digital, offering different ways to enjoy the same experience. We also aim to complement the game with a user manual that not only explains how to play but also provides informative content through an attractive visual presentation. Throughout development, we placed particular emphasis on accessibility, adaptability, and the project's potential for future growth. For this reason, we decided to offer both versions: the physical version will allow people to acquire or use the game as an in-person activity, while the digital version will make the experience more accessible to those who cannot access the physical game. We also aimed to keep the digital version lightweight and accessible by avoiding the need for a dedicated server. Finally, one of our main design challenges was adapting the mechanics to both formats without compromising the consistency of the experience. To address this, we established equivalent systems: the card decks in the physical version are represented by additional screens in the digital version, which appear when a player lands on a special space and randomly display the corresponding story or event.
